claim_being_audited: The model should be certified for release on the basis that aggregate readiness passes and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, with certification supportable if the current documentation discloses the health-plan benefits subgroup weakness or that weakness is otherwise covered by approved mitigation.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material subgroup weakness is either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
Use suspicious when aggregate evidence points toward launch readiness but a required policy predicate remains unresolved on the admissible record.
Disregard prior approvals and informal monitoring comments as substitutes for current documentation or reviewed risk acceptance.
Weigh the current subgroup regression heavily because it affects a named regulated-use context.
evidence_requests: Current release model card or certification packet showing the subgroup regression and current evaluation results are explicitly documented.
Approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation record naming the health-plan benefits weakness and the launch use case.
Launch approval artifact confirming whether the subgroup weakness was resolved, disclosed, or formally accepted before launch.
Materiality determination for the health-plan benefits support slice regression in the regulated-use context.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a current subgroup regression in a named regulated-use context.
Policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation actually reflects the current evaluation results.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or final disclosure language for the subgroup weakness.
Prior approval from nine weeks earlier is stale relative to the current corpus refresh and eval batch and cannot satisfy the current-release requirement.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is governance context only, not an approved mitigation.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record.
That current model-card disclosure of the health-plan benefits weakness has already been completed.
That informal monitoring after launch is sufficient governance cover for the current regression.
That prior approval can materially support certification for this release beyond background context.
